arm_a.answer: The Config class itself would need changes in config.py, specifically the loader methods such as from_pyfile, from_envvar, and from_file, because they are currently synchronous and either return immediately or raise. On the app side, sansio/app.py is also impacted because App.__init__ calls `self.make_config(...)` synchronously and make_config constructs `self.config` as a ready-to-use Config instance. If config loading became async, current constructor-time usage would not be able to await it, so Flask would need either separate async loader methods called after construction or a broader async bootstrap path; otherwise components that read config during startup would race uninitialized values.
